key_insight: CoRe-WM learns evolving breast MRI response states to predict pathologic complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, rather than learning representations directly from outcome labels.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support treatment-response assessment at successive imaging visits, but clinical benefit has not been established.
method: Predicts the next latent imaging state from longitudinal breast DCE-MRI.
Conditions state transitions on patient clinical profiles and assigned therapy while separating response dynamics from imaging appearance.
Freezes the pretrained model and trains a linear readout to predict pathologic complete response.
evidence_signal: In five-fold cross-validation on I-SPY2, CoRe-WM showed the highest discrimination among evaluated methods at every prospective decision point; transfer was also assessed on I-SPY1.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance estimates, and prospective clinical validation is needed before use in treatment decisions.
paper_title: CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI
